title: The FCC bans all robot vacuums made outside the U.S.
excerpt: That's pretty much all of them.
content_html:
Credit: skaman306 / Getty Images

The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned all foreign-made mobile robots from the country — including robot vacuums. This means that people in the U.S. won't be able to get new robot vacuums from brands such as Roborock, Ecovacs, Dreame, and Samsung.

On Tuesday, the FCC announced that it has added "advanced robotic devices" made outside the U.S. to its Covered List. This list documents communications equipment and services that the U.S. government believes pose an "unacceptable risk" to national security. Products on the Covered List are prohibited from receiving FCC equipment authorisation, which is mandatory for most electronic devices imported or sold within the country. 

As such, this update means that foreign-manufactured advanced robotic devices cannot be imported or sold in the U.S. The FCC's announcement specifically mentioned limbed robots such as humanoids and quadrupeds, leaving no doubt that tech such as XPENG's humanoid IRON robot and Unitree's Go2 Pro Robot Dog will be barred from the country. 

You May Also Like

However, robot vacuums also neatly fit within the ban's scope. As cited by the FCC, the National Security Determination defines "advanced robotic devices" as:

A mechanical mobile device, including autonomous mobile robots, humanoid robots, and quadrupeds, that – 

i. Is capable of locomotion, obstacle avoidance, navigation, or movement on the ground;

ii. Operates at a distance from a human operator or supervisor based on commands or in response to sensor data or any combination thereof; and 

iii. The combined weight of the device and, if applicable, ground station or docking station is over 4.4lbs; and 

iv. Contains a component falling within each of the below subparagraphs: 

i. a sensor capable of perceiving its environment; 

ii. a component that is capable of providing network connectivity (wired or wireless, including Bluetooth/WiFi, cellular, or satellite) with connection speeds of at least 200 kbps in either direction; and 

iii. software running either locally or remotely, including firmware and AI or machine-learning model weights, that controls the robot’s autonomous navigation or movement perception, data collection, or remote command-and-control

Such features are integral to robot vacuums' operations, which require them to independently navigate areas in order to clean them. The FCC has since confirmed that the U.S. ban does include robot vacuums, as reported by The Verge. 

Mashable has reached out to Roborock, Ecovacs, Dreame, and Samsung. At the time of writing only Roborock has responded, and they declined to comment.

Mashable Light Speed

The National Security Determination also specifically referred to an incident involving a robot vacuum when outlining the U.S. government's concerns. Earlier this year, a software engineer accidentally hacked his DJI Romo robot vacuum and gained access to video, audio, and map data from thousands of devices across the world. (DJI devices have already been barred from the U.S. for some time, the government having classified it as a "'Chinese military company.")

Security vulnerabilities such as this aren't exclusive to foreign-made devices, and aren't necessarily an indication of sinister intentions. U.S. companies such as Amazon, Meta, and Uber have all experienced their own safety and security incidents as well. No technology is infallible, regardless of where it was made or who it was made by. Even so, the U.S. government considers such incidents in foreign technology as demonstrative of a national security threat.

"The networked capabilities of advanced robotic systems create extensive vulnerabilities and vectors for attacks that can manipulate the data and physical operation of the advanced robotic system," the National Security Determination reads. "Relying on foreign-produced advanced robotic devices presents unacceptable supply chain and cybersecurity vulnerabilities."

Fortunately, the U.S. robot vacuum ban won't force you to throw out your current device. The FCC states that consumers are still allowed to use devices they already own, so there's no need to rush out to look for a replacement. The ban doesn't revoke FCC authorisation from previously approved devices either, meaning those in the U.S. can continue to buy and sell robot vacuum models that are already in the market. 

However, new robot vacuums that have not yet received FCC authorisation are now barred from entering the country, leaving U.S. consumers with older models and significantly fewer options. The vast majority of robot vacuums are made outside the U.S., with the top five manufacturers based in China. Combined, these five companies held almost 70 percent of the global robot vacuum market share as of 2025. 

In comparison, the U.S. has practically no robot vacuum companies. While Roomba maker iRobot was founded in California, the company filed for bankruptcy last year and was acquired by Chinese robotics company Picea.

The Department of War (DOW) and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) are authorised to grant exemptions to the U.S. robotics ban upon conducting a national security assessment. However, the FCC does not list any at time of writing.

Earlier this year, the FCC banned all foreign-made consumer-level WiFi routers, also labelling them a danger to national security. The vast majority of routers are manufactured outside the U.S., including those from trusted brands such as TP-Link, ASUS, and Netgear.

Assistant Editor

content_html_zh:
图片来源：skaman306 / Getty Images

美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）已禁止所有外国制造的移动机器人进入该国，包括扫地机器人。 这意味着美国人将无法从 Roborock、Ecovacs、Dreame 和 Samsung 等品牌获得新的扫地机器人。

周二，美国联邦通信委员会宣布已将美国境外制造的“先进机器人设备”添加到其涵盖清单中。 该清单记录了美国政府认为对国家安全构成“不可接受的风险”的通信设备和服务。 涵盖清单上的产品禁止获得 FCC 设备授权，这对于在该国进口或销售的大多数电子设备是强制性的。

因此，此次更新意味着外国制造的先进机器人设备不能在美国进口或销售。FCC的公告特别提到了人形和四足动物等肢体机器人，毫无疑问，小鹏的人形IRON机器人和Unitree的Go2 Pro机器狗等技术将被禁止进入该国。

你可能也喜欢

然而，机器人吸尘器也完全符合禁令的范围。 正如美国联邦通信委员会 (FCC) 所引用的，国家安全决定将“先进机器人设备”定义为：

一种机械移动设备，包括自主移动机器人、人形机器人和四足机器人，即 – i. 能够在地面上移动、避障、导航或移动；ii． 根据命令或响应传感器数据或其任意组合，在距操作员或主管一定距离的地方进行操作；和 iii. 设备和地面站或扩展坞（如果适用）的总重量超过 4.4 磅；和四． 包含属于以下各小段的组件： 能够感知周围环境的传感器；二. 能够提供网络连接（有线或无线，包括蓝牙/WiFi、蜂窝或卫星）的组件，任一方向的连接速度至少为 200 kbps；和 iii. 在本地或远程运行的软件，包括固件和人工智能或机器学习模型权重，用于控制机器人的自主导航或运动感知、数据收集或远程命令和控制

这些功能是机器人吸尘器操作不可或缺的一部分，这要求它们独立导航区域以进行清洁。 据 The Verge 报道，美国联邦通信委员会随后证实，美国的禁令确实包括扫地机器人。

Mashable 已与 Roborock、Ecovacs、Dreame 和 Samsung 取得联系。 截至撰写本文时，只有 Roborock 做出了回应，但他们拒绝发表评论。

可混搭光速

国家安全决定在概述美国政府的担忧时还特别提到了涉及机器人吸尘器的事件。 今年早些时候，一名软件工程师意外侵入了他的 DJI Romo 扫地机器人，并获得了来自全球数千台设备的视频、音频和地图数据的访问权限。 （大疆设备已被禁止进入美国一段时间，政府将其归类为“中国军事公司”。）

诸如此类的安全漏洞并非外国制造的设备所独有，也不一定表明存在险恶意图。 亚马逊、Meta 和 Uber 等美国公司也都经历过自己的安全事件。 没有任何技术是绝对正确的，无论它是在哪里制造的或由谁制造的。 即便如此，美国政府仍认为外国技术中的此类事件表明了国家安全威胁。

国家安全决定写道：“先进机器人系统的网络功能创造了广泛的漏洞和攻击媒介，可以操纵先进机器人系统的数据和物理操作。” “依赖外国生产的先进机器人设备会带来不可接受的供应链和网络安全漏洞。”

幸运的是，美国的机器人真空禁令不会迫使你扔掉你当前的设备。 FCC 表示，消费者仍然可以使用他们已经拥有的设备，因此无需急于寻找替代品。 该禁令也不会撤销 FCC 对之前批准的设备的授权，这意味着美国人可以继续购买和销售市场上已有的扫地机器人型号。

然而，尚未获得 FCC 授权的新型扫地机器人现在被禁止进入该国，这使得美国消费者只能使用较旧的型号，并且选择也大大减少。 绝大多数扫地机器人都是在美国境外生产的，其中排名前五的制造商都位于中国。 截至 2025 年，这五家公司合计占据全球扫地机器人市场近 70% 的份额。

相比之下，美国几乎没有扫地机器人公司。 虽然 Roomba 制造商 iRobot 成立于加利福尼亚州，但该公司去年申请破产，并被中国机器人公司 Picea 收购。

战争部 (DOW) 和国土安全部 (DHS) 有权在进行国家安全评估后授予美国机器人禁令豁免。 然而，在撰写本文时，FCC 尚未列出任何内容。

今年早些时候，美国联邦通信委员会禁止所有外国制造的消费级 WiFi 路由器，并将其标记为对国家安全的威胁。 绝大多数路由器都是在美国境外制造的，包括来自 TP-Link、华硕和 Netgear 等值得信赖的品牌的路由器。
